Part of my job is to investigate and resolve disputes that customers report to the bank I work for. Most online card transactions are processed through VISA, MasterCard, or whatever major logo is on the face of your credit / debit card. Recently (Within the last 2 years) PayPal has started processing transactions through a non-branded network, meaning the primary logo on your card is not involved in the transaction. This saves PayPal money because they don't have to pay those network fees, but they also don't have to follow regulations and guidelines in resolving disputes that those card brands have put in place.

This means if you ordered something and didn't receive it, or got the wrong item, or returned it but never received a credit to your account, PayPal can deny that claim without providing any proof or correcting the error.

TL;DR - PayPal has been getting scummier and scummier, for both the consumer and merchant side of payment processing. I would highly advise finding an alternate service, PayPal is not on your side or looking out for your best interests.
PSA: PayPal sucks. Not only are they freezing accounts along with funds in them, recently they have started processing outside of major card brands to avoid their consumer protections.
